classification.difficultyReason: Infer an obtuse included angle, find two route lengths and combine the round-trip distance.

content.prompt:
A salesman drove from town $A$ to town $B$, then to town $C$, then finally directly home to town $A$.
Town B is 67 km north of town $A$, and the bearings of town $C$ from towns $A$ and $B$ are $039^\circ\mathrm{T}$ and $063^\circ\mathrm{T}$ respectively. Find how far the salesman drove, correct to the nearest kilometre.

spec.description: Monochrome triangle ABC: vertical AB at left with A below B; C above-right of B. AB is labelled 67 km on its left. A dashed north extension above B ends in an arrowhead without North text. Italic A below-left, B left and C right. Interior 39-degree label at A and exterior 63-degree label between BC and the north extension at B; no visible angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: AB=67 km; bearing AC=039 degrees; bearing BC=063 degrees. Labels are positioned by angle pics without drawing additional arcs.
